question: Explain why increasing the frequency of incident radiation increases the maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons, while increasing intensity increases only the number of emitted photoelectrons.

options.A: Since each photon has energy $h\nu$, increasing frequency raises $K_{\max}=h\nu-\phi_0$. At fixed frequency, greater intensity means more photons per second, so more photoelectrons are emitted but the energy of each photon remains unchanged.
options.B: Increasing intensity raises the energy of each photon and therefore increases stopping potential, while frequency only changes the number of electrons.
options.C: Both frequency and intensity affect only the work function of the metal.
options.D: Increasing frequency increases photoelectric current only, whereas intensity increases maximum kinetic energy.
